A1-characteristics-of-living-things

A neat 4 by 2 grid of eight separate small icon illustrations, evenly spaced with generous white space between them and below each one (no boxes or frames). Top row left to right: a goat running; a pair of human lungs; a plate of food (rice, beans and plantain); a hand pulling back quickly from a small candle flame. Bottom row left to right: a young maize (corn) plant growing taller in three stages; a single human kidney; a hen with three small chicks; a wilted, drooping dead plant in a pot.
A1-animal-cell

A single typical animal cell (like a human cheek cell) shown as a 2D cut-away diagram, rounded irregular outline. Inside, clearly separate and well-spaced: a thin cell membrane, pale cytoplasm, one large round nucleus with a visible double nuclear membrane and a dark nucleolus inside it, several bean-shaped mitochondria with inner folds, a network of rough endoplasmic reticulum near the nucleus with tiny dots (ribosomes), a Golgi body as a stack of curved flattened sacs, a few small vacuoles, a couple of small round lysosomes, and a pair of centrioles (two small cylinders at right angles) near the nucleus. Each organelle distinct and easy to point to.
A1-plant-cell

A single typical plant cell (like a leaf palisade cell) shown as a 2D cut-away diagram, regular rectangular shape standing upright. A thick outer cell wall, a thin cell membrane just inside it, a very large central vacuole filling most of the cell, a thin layer of cytoplasm around the edges, a nucleus pushed against one side with a nucleolus, many green oval chloroplasts lining the cytoplasm, a few bean-shaped mitochondria, a small Golgi body (stack of curved sacs), a short piece of endoplasmic reticulum with tiny ribosome dots. Each organelle distinct and well spaced so it is easy to point to.
A1-plant-vs-animal-cell

Two cells side by side with clear white space between them, drawn at the same scale. LEFT: a typical plant cell, rectangular, with a thick bright green cell wall around the outside, a thin membrane inside it, a very large central vacuole, several green oval chloroplasts around the edge, a nucleus to one side and a few mitochondria. RIGHT: a typical animal cell, rounded and irregular, with a thin cell membrane, a central nucleus, mitochondria, small vacuoles and a pair of bright orange centrioles (two small cylinders at right angles) near the nucleus. Use soft muted colours for shared parts so the plant-only parts (cell wall, chloroplasts, large vacuole) stand out in green and the centrioles stand out in orange.
A1-levels-of-organisation

A left-to-right flow of five pictures in one horizontal row, evenly spaced, each connected to the next by a simple plain arrow: 1) a single spindle-shaped heart muscle cell with a nucleus; 2) a small block of muscle tissue made of many such cells; 3) a human heart (organ) drawn simply; 4) the human circulatory system: a simple outline torso with the heart and red and blue blood vessels branching through it; 5) a whole smiling Nigerian teenage boy standing (the organism). Keep plenty of white space above and below the row.
A1-euglena-paramecium

Two single-celled organisms side by side, each clearly separated with white space between them. LEFT: Euglena, a spindle-shaped green cell with one long whip-like flagellum coming out of the front end, a red-orange eyespot near the front, many small green chloroplasts, a round nucleus in the middle, a contractile vacuole near the front, and a thin flexible outer pellicle with faint spiral stripes. RIGHT: Paramecium, a slipper-shaped cell covered all over its edge with fine short cilia, an oral groove indented on one side, several round food vacuoles, one large bean-shaped macronucleus with a small round micronucleus beside it, and two star-shaped contractile vacuoles, one near each end.
A1-epithelial-tissues

Four small panels side by side in one row, separated by white space (no frames), each showing a simple cross-section of a type of epithelial tissue sitting on a thin dark basement membrane line: 1) squamous epithelium: one layer of thin flat tile-like cells with flat nuclei; 2) cuboidal epithelium: one layer of cube-shaped cells with round central nuclei; 3) columnar epithelium: one layer of tall column cells with oval nuclei near the base; 4) ciliated columnar epithelium: tall column cells with tiny hair-like cilia on top. Soft pink and purple tones.
A1-hydra

A longitudinal section (cut lengthways) through a Hydra, a small freshwater animal, standing upright with its basal disc attached to the stem of a water plant at the bottom. Show: a ring of long slender tentacles at the top around a raised cone (hypostome) with a mouth opening at its tip; a hollow central body cavity (enteron) running down the body; a body wall of two cell layers, an outer ectoderm and an inner endoderm, separated by a thin jelly-like layer (mesoglea) between them; a small bud growing out from one side of the body with its own tiny tentacles; the basal disc at the bottom. Soft greens and blues.
A1-onion-bulb

A longitudinal section (cut lengthways) through an onion bulb, upright. Show: a flattened disc-shaped stem at the base; a tuft of thin adventitious roots hanging from the underside of the disc; many thick fleshy scale leaves wrapped in layers around the centre; thin dry papery brown outer scale leaves on the outside; a terminal bud (pale young shoot) in the centre rising from the disc; one small axillary bud between two scale leaves near the base. Soft purples, creams and browns.
A1-chlamydomonas

A single Chlamydomonas cell, a tiny oval green alga, shown large and upright. Two equal long whip-like flagella come out of the front (top) end. A thin clear cell wall around the outside. A large cup-shaped green chloroplast filling the bottom and sides of the cell, with one round pyrenoid inside the base of the cup. A small red eyespot on the side of the chloroplast near the front. Two small contractile vacuoles near the base of the flagella. A round nucleus sitting inside the hollow of the cup. Soft greens.
